page.text:
Welcome to **Mathlore**, a structured mathematical library and encyclopedia
constructed from first principles using the **Mathlingua** language.

The goal of Mathlore is to provide an accessible, rigorous, and structurally-checked
foundation for mathematics—spanning symbolic logic, axiomatic set theory, relations,
function theory, number systems, and abstract algebra.

page.text:
Set theory is the foundational substrate of classical mathematics. In this
system, mathematical objects—from natural numbers to functions and algebraic
structures—are constructed as sets obeying the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms.
The theory proceeds from the primitive membership relation $\in$ through
subsets, products, and standard Boolean operations.

page.text:
The natural numbers represent the arithmetic foundation of counting. This section
develops the natural numbers abstractly through the Peano postulates—introducing
recursive arithmetic and order—and provides their canonical set-theoretic
realization as the Von Neumann finite ordinals $\omega$.

page.text:
Abstract algebra investigates sets equipped with operations, establishing theorems
that depend solely on operational properties rather than the concrete nature of
elements. This chapter ascends the algebraic ladder from magmas, semigroups, and
monoids to groups, and culminates in rings and fields.

page.text:
Linear algebra studies vector spaces and the structure-preserving linear maps
between them. It forms the geometric and computational bedrock of modern
mathematics and applied science, providing the algebraic language of linear
systems, coordinate transformations, matrices, and spectral decompositions.

page.text:
Real analysis is the rigorous theory of functions of a real variable and
the geometry of the continuum. Grounded in the completeness property of
the real numbers, it establishes the formal foundations of limits,
infinite series, continuous mappings, differentiation, and integration.

page.text:
Complex analysis is the study of complex numbers and holomorphic functions.
Endowed with geometric elegance and algebraic rigidity, complex differentiability
unfolds into conformality, the Cauchy-Riemann equations, contour integration,
and the powerful calculus of residues.
